full_caption: Blackthorn Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc., Appellant, v. Larkspur Hill Holdings, LLC, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Blackthorn Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc. claims title by adverse possession to a 17.3-acre wooded tract adjoining 4720 Old Quarry Turnpike, Pinecrest, NR, of which Larkspur Hill Holdings, LLC is the record owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: Continuity is broken by an entry of the record owner made with intent to reclaim possession. The single survey visit by Larkspur Hill Holdings, LLC's agent in 2018, unaccompanied by any assertion of possession, did not interrupt the running of the statute.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: Hostility does not require ill will. It requires only that the possession be without the record owner's permission and inconsistent with the owner's title. A claimant's mistaken belief as to the true line does not defeat hostility in this State.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: The trial court found the elements satisfied as to 40.2 acres and not satisfied as to the remainder, which lay beyond any fence or posted line. That allocation is not clearly erroneous.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: Land held by a municipality for a public purpose is not subject to adverse possession. The 50-foot strip within the platted right of way is therefore excluded from any judgment in Blackthorn Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc.'s favor.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Possession is 'actual' where the claimant uses the land as an ordinary owner of similar land would use it. For wooded acreage, selective timbering, posting, and seasonal recreational use may suffice where cultivation would not be expected.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: Blackthorn Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc. posted the tract against trespass in 1988, cut and sold standing timber in 1998 and 2014, and maintained a hunting camp on the northeast quarter continuously thereafter.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Tacking is permitted between successive possessors in privity. Blackthorn Ridge Homeowners Association, Inc. may tack the 4 years of possession by its predecessor, whose deed purported to convey the disputed tract, to satisfy the statutory term.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Adverse possession requires possession that is actual, open and notorious, exclusive, hostile, and continuous for the statutory period of 21 years. Each element must be established by clear and convincing evidence.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: Affirmed in part, reversed in part, and remanded for entry of a decree describing the vested tract by metes and bounds consistent with the surveyor's Exhibit A.

sections.heading: RIDER 2 — ACTS OF POSSESSION RELIED UPON
sections.text: Claimant relies upon the following acts, each continuing from the date shown through the date of filing: posting of the perimeter against trespass beginning in 1988; commercial timber harvest in 1998 and 2014; construction and continuous seasonal use of a hunting camp; annual maintenance of the interior access track; and payment of the real property taxes assessed against the tract for 15 of the 21 years preceding this claim.

sections.heading: RIDER 4 — EXCLUSIONS FROM CLAIM
sections.text: This claim expressly excludes: (a) any land held by the municipality or the State for a public purpose, including the 50-foot platted right of way; (b) any land subject to a recorded easement, as to which Claimant asserts no interest inconsistent with the easement; and (c) any subsurface mineral estate previously severed of record.

sections.heading: RIDER 5 — QUIET TITLE RELIEF REQUESTED
sections.text: Claimant requests a decree quieting title in Claimant as against Respondent and all persons claiming under Respondent, describing the vested tract by metes and bounds, directing the Recorder to index the decree against both parcels, and awarding costs. Claimant does not seek damages for the period of possession.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Recording
sections.text: This instrument shall be recorded in the land records of Pinecrest County, Northridge, and shall run with the land, binding upon and inuring to the benefit of the parties and their respective heirs, successors, personal representatives and assigns. The party causing the instrument to be recorded shall bear the recording fees and shall furnish a conformed copy to the other party within 15 days of recording.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Force Majeure
sections.text: Neither party shall be liable for a failure of performance, other than an obligation to pay money, caused by an act of God, flood, fire, civil disturbance, governmental order, epidemic, or other cause beyond that party's reasonable control, provided the affected party gives notice within 15 days and resumes performance as promptly as practicable.

sections.heading: Clause 3 — Interpretation and Construction Against Drafter
sections.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect construction. The singular includes the plural. This instrument is the product of negotiation between the parties, and no rule of construction requiring interpretation against the drafting party shall apply. Restrictions on the use of land shall nonetheless be construed in favor of the free use of the land.
